outline.text: Leverage fell by 0.3x in the year. Almost all of it came from EBITDA growth; net debt rose after the Corvane Fasteners purchase.
Working capital absorbed USD 71m as inventory was built for the engine ramp. Free cash flow covered interest but little else.
Pricing power sits in the aftermarket
Sole-source parts carry most of the profit. Original-equipment contracts are fixed-price and thinner than peers.
The 2028 notes are the first real test
The term loan and secured notes run to 2030 and 2031. The unsecured notes come first and rank behind both.
Only a springing first-lien covenant applies, and only when the facility is more than 40% drawn. It is far from tested.

outline.text: A sole-source aftermarket franchise carries a thinner original-equipment business.
Build rates are rising; pricing discipline among the three large suppliers is holding.
Revenue up 7%, margin up 0.6 points, both ahead of the prior run.
Liquidity is adequate for eighteen months; conversion is the weak point.
Secured debt is long-dated; the unsecured notes mature first.
One springing covenant, untested, with wide baskets.
Sponsor-controlled board; a record of debt-funded purchases.
More levered than four of five peers, with the highest margin.
The security package documents were not among the files provided, so recovery by class could not be assessed.
Both agencies stable; one upgrade trigger is within reach by 2027.
No finding that changes the credit view.
Base case reaches 4.1x by September 2027; downside stays at 4.8x.
A one-page summary of this run for committee papers.
Recovery by class was not assessable: the security and intercreditor documents were not provided.
The hedge schedule was not in the files, so the fixed and floating split of interest is an estimate and hedge expiries are not established for this run.
Peer figures for two companies are on a reported basis while Halden is company-adjusted; the comparison overstates Halden by an amount the module could not size.
EBITDA for 2022 is not available on the current basis, so five-year trends start in 2023.
